newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: APB expects lower second half profit.
newsitem.headline: APB expects lower second half profit.

text.p: Asia-Pacific Breweries Ltd said on Friday it expected profits for the second half to be significantly lower than the same period a year ago due to start-up losses at its Hainan and Cambodian breweries.
The company said in a statement accompanying its first half results that it expected a reduction in its full year profit, compared with the previous year.
The group posted a 14.4 percent rise in net profit to Singapore $49.46 million for the six months ended March 31, 1997.

It said earnings growth in Singapore, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Malaysia and Thailand was partly offset by lower profitability in Vietnam, which suffered from higher depreciation costs and currency devaluation.
Results were also affected by start-up losses at a new brewery in Cambodia, which was commissioned in October 1996.
